pages.title: Molecular Orbital Lattice
pages.text: Electron clouds shared across a whole grid of atoms, frozen in place so I can finally see what a bond is: not a stick between balls but a wavefunction spread over both, lower in energy than either alone. The lattice shimmers faintly where the orbitals overlap.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Solving the Schrodinger equation for a molecule taught me where the electrons sit. I used a qubit to encode that solution and grew the crystal around it on a zeolite template in supercritical solvent, so the orbitals set exactly where the mathematics put them.

Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$() and $(item)Quantum Computer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carbon Nanotube Bundle, Chiral Crystal, Folded Protein Crystal, Gene Sequencer.
